ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: A blight is in the fields of {PEOPLE}.

lines.li: [them] The blight is in our fields at {SITUATIONPLACE}, and it moves a row a day.
[us] Is there anything that stops it?
[them,their:lowtech] Cutting out the sick rows and burning them, and hoping the wind stays down.
[them] Cutting out every sick row and burning it before it reaches the next field.
[us] Then we'll watch our own rows closely.
[them] Look every morning, it shows on the underside of the leaves first.
[them] Have you heard about the blight in the fields at {HEARDPLACE}?
[us] Only that it's bad there.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} are burning whole rows of it, and grain is getting dear on the road.
[us] Then we'd better look after our own fields.
[them] The blight has gone out of our fields at last.
[us] What did it leave you?
[them] Burnt rows and a thin harvest, and seed we'll buy from someone else next year.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: Summer has not come to the fields of {PEOPLE}.

lines.li: [them] There was frost on our fields again this week, in the middle of summer.
[us] How are the crops taking it?
[them] They stand yellow and short, and half of them won't ripen at all.
[us] Have the old people seen a year like this before?
[them,their:tribal] The eldest says her grandmother told of one, and it was a hungry winter after.
[them] None of them have, and they're the ones most worried.
[them] They say summer never came at {HEARDPLACE} this year.
[us] We'd heard it's been cold out that way.
[them] Theirs is worse, {HEARDPEOPLE} had frost at haymaking time.
[us] That will mean a hard winter for them.
[them] For them, and for anyone who buys their grain.
[them] The cold year is behind us, if not the hunger it left.
[us] Did you get anything in from the fields?
[them] Some, and we'll be eating it very carefully until the next harvest.
[them] There's no drink to be had at {SITUATIONPLACE} just now, by order.
[us] What brought that on?
[them,their:lowtech] A feast that ended in a fight, so the elders broke the brewing jars.
[them] A celebration that ended in a fight, and now nobody may sell a drop.
[us] How is the town taking it?
[them] The old ones agree with it, and the young ones are looking for someone who sells.
[them] Did you know {HEARDPEOPLE} have banned drink at {HEARDPLACE}?
[us] The whole town?
[them] The whole town, and some of the young ones are looking for anyone who'll sell.
[us] There's always someone who will.
[them] The ban on drink is over at home.
[us] Was it lifted, or did it just stop being kept?
[them] A bit of both, and nobody is in a hurry to say which.
[them] {SITUATION} is on its way to {SITUATIONPLACE}, and the whole town is waiting for it.
[us] What does it carry?
[them,their:lowtech] Cloth and salt from beyond the mountains, and things we have no name for.
[them] Goods from beyond the mountains that we haven't seen in two years.
[us] I hope it gets there safely.
[them] So does everyone, and the bandits are hoping the other thing.
[them] {HEARD} is crossing the region, bound for {HEARDPLACE}.
[us] We've heard it's a big one.
[them] Big enough that half the traders on the road are following it to see what it sells.
[us] And the other half?
[them] Watching out for the bandits who are following it too.
[them] {ENDED} is over, and the road to our town is quiet again.
[us] Did your town get what it waited for?
[them] Less than we hoped and more than we feared, as these things go.
[them] We're building {SITUATION} at {SITUATIONPLACE}, the whole town is on it.
[us] That's a big undertaking.
[them] The biggest anyone can remember, and the timber is running short already.
[us] Will it be finished this season?
[them,them:old] I hope to see it finished, at my age that's not a small hope.
[them] If the timber comes, and if the master builder's temper holds.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} are raising {HEARD} at {HEARDPLACE}, have you heard?
[us] We've heard they want timber for it.
[them] They want timber, stone and anyone who can swing a hammer.
[us] I'd like to see it when it's done.
[them] The work on {ENDED} is over, one way or another.
[us] Did it get finished?
[them] Come and see it, I'd rather you judged for yourself.
[them] Has {SITUATION} come anywhere near your land?
[us] Not that we've seen, though we've heard plenty about it.
[them,situation:theirs] It's been seen in the hills above our town, and nobody goes out alone now.
[them] Everyone has a story about it, and the tracks are bigger in every telling.
[us] Is anyone going after it?
[them] A few want to, and the rest are hoping it moves on by itself.
[them] They're talking about {HEARD} at every fire on the road.
[us] Have you seen it yourself?
[them] No, and from what I hear, I'm glad of it.
[us] Where was it last seen?
[them] Somewhere near {HEARDPLACE}, but it never stays long in one place.
[them] Nobody talks of {ENDED} on the road anymore.
[us] What became of it?
[them] Ask three people and you'll get three answers, but it's gone from the hills.
[them] There's hardly any medicine left at {SITUATIONPLACE}.
[us] What are your healers doing without it?
[them,their:lowtech] Clean cloth, boiled water and a lot of prayer.
[them] Rationing what's left for the worst cases and sending the rest home to rest.
[us] I hope nobody falls badly ill until it's over.
[them] So do we, it's a bad time to break a leg.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} at {HEARDPLACE} are short of medicine, I hear.
[us] Badly?
[them] Badly enough that a bundle of healroot sells there for a week's wages.
[us] Then I'm glad of what we have.
[them] Medicine is coming up the road to us again.
[us] That must be a relief to your healers.
[them,ended:helped] It is, and they haven't forgotten whose medicine got them through.
[them] It is, and they've put a little by in case it happens again.
[them] Our people are caught up in {SITUATION}, as you'll have heard.
[us] We have, and we're sorry for it.
[them,their:lowtech] It started over a line on the ground, and now there are burned barns on both sides.
[them] It started over a line on a map, and now both sides have called up their fighters.
[us] Do you think it will end soon?
[them] Not before the season does, and maybe not then.
[them] Have you heard how {HEARD} is going?
[us] Only that it hasn't ended.
[them] The road past {HEARDPLACE} is full of soldiers, and the traders go the long way round.
[us] We'll keep well out of it.
[them] Wise, both sides are looking for friends just now.
[them] {ENDED} is over, and our fighters are home.
[us] Did it settle anything?
[them] Not much, but both sides are tired of it, and that's enough for now.
[them] Our new town at {SITUATIONPLACE} is finished, or finished enough to live in.
[us] What does it still need?
[them] Everything at once, but timber most of all.
[us] It's good to have new neighbors.
[them] Come and see it when the roofs are all on.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} have a new town at {HEARDPLACE}, did you know?
[us] We've heard something of it.
[them] It's mostly mud and scaffolding so far, but they're proud of it.
[us] Every town starts like that.
[them] Our new town has found its feet.
[us] Is it what you hoped?
[them] It has a market and a well that doesn't run dry, so it's close enough.
[them] Some of our young ones have gone off to ride with the warlord's son.
[us] Does that worry you?
[them] Their mothers are sick about it, and so is anyone with sense.
[us] We'd rather not see any of them at our walls.
[them] Nor would we, but they don't listen to us anymore.
[them] They say the warlord's son has raised a band and is camped somewhere near you.
[us] We've heard the same.
[them] Then keep someone watching the hills, he hasn't forgotten his father.
[us] We'll watch, thank you for the warning.
[them] Nobody on the road talks of the warlord's son now.
[us] Good, we've had enough of that family.
[them] Most people have, one way or another.
[them] There's a war band camped in the woods above {SITUATIONPLACE}.
[us] That town was ours once.
[them] We know, and the people there mean to keep it standing.
[us] How many are there?
[them] More every night, and they don't hide their fires.
[them] I hear raiders are camped above {HEARDPLACE}, the town that was yours.
[us] We've heard it too.
[them] The people there say they'll hold, and people always say that.
[us] We hope they're right.
[them] The trouble at the town that was yours is over.
[us] We've been thinking of the people there.
[them] They'll be glad to hear it, it was a hard few weeks.
[them] Whole households of ours are on the road to {SITUATIONPLACE}.
[us] Why are they leaving home?
[them] The fields out there have been dry too long to feed them.
[us] Is there land for them where they're going?
[them] Their kin have promised it, and they'll hold them to the promise.
[them] I passed a long line of {HEARDPEOPLE}'s households on the road.
[us] Moving to {HEARDPLACE}, we heard.
[them] Old and young, with everything they own on carts and on their backs.
[us] It's a hard way to start over.
[them] The last of our households has reached the new land.
[us] Are they settling in?
[them] Slowly, it takes a while before a new place feels like yours.
[them] The stores at {SITUATIONPLACE} are nearly empty, and the next harvest is a long way off.
[us] How are people managing?
[them,their:tribal] The hunters go out every day, and the old ones eat last.
[them] One meal a day, and the children get the larger share.
[us] I'm sorry, I hope the next harvest is a good one.
[them] So do we, it has to be.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} are going hungry at {HEARDPLACE}, I'm told.
[us] We'd heard their harvest failed.
[them] It did, and grain costs a small fortune there now.
[us] That will be hard on the poorer families.
[them] It is, they're the ones eating the seed corn.
[them] The worst of the hunger is over at home.
[us] I'm glad to hear it.
[them,ended:helped] We won't forget who sent food when we had none.
[them] So are we, though some of us won't waste a crumb again.
[them] {SITUATION} is in half the houses at {SITUATIONPLACE}.
[us] Are you well yourself?
[them] Well enough, I've kept away from the sick and washed my hands raw.
[us] Who looks after the ones who have it?
[them,their:healers] The order's sickhouse is full, and the healers sleep in turns.
[them] Their families, mostly, and the healers when they can get there.
[them] {HEARD} is going round {HEARDPLACE}, did you know?
[us] We'd heard there was sickness there.
[them] I went the long way round to keep clear of it.
[us] We'll be careful with travelers from that way.
[them] {ENDED} has burned itself out at home.
[us] How is the town now?
[them] Tired, and glad to open the doors again.
[them] The snow at {SITUATIONPLACE} is up to the windows this winter.
[us] Do you have enough to burn?
[them,their:lowtech] We're burning the fence posts, and next it'll be the furniture.
[them] Not enough, and the fuel carts can't get through the drifts.
[us] It can't last forever.
[them] It only has to last a few more weeks to do a lot of harm.
[them] They say {HEARDPLACE} is snowed in, nothing gets in or out.
[us] We'd heard the winter was hard out there.
[them] Theirs is worse, {HEARDPEOPLE} are burning anything that will burn.
[us] I hope they make it to the spring.
[them] The thaw has come at home, finally.
[us] How bad was it at the end?
[them] Bad, but the roads are open and the woodpiles can be built up again.
[them] There isn't a bolt of cloth to be had at {SITUATIONPLACE}.
[us] What happened to it?
[them,their:lowtech] The weavers ran out of thread, and the traders stopped bringing any.
[them] The mill that sent it stopped, and nobody else makes enough.
[us] What are people wearing?
[them] Last year's clothes, patched until you can't see what they were.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} will pay almost anything for cloth at {HEARDPLACE} just now.
[us] Is it that scarce?
[them] They're cutting down old cloaks to make clothes for the children.
[us] Then we'll look after the clothes we have.
[them] There's cloth at home again, and the tailors are busy.
[us] Everyone wanting new clothes at once?
[them] Everyone, and the children most of all, they've grown out of everything.
[them] Nobody at {SITUATIONPLACE} can get timber for love or money.
[us] Is there nothing left in the woods?
[them] Nothing near enough to haul, and the carpenters are idle half the week.
[us] What happens to the building work?
[them] It waits, and so do the families who need a roof.
[them] At {HEARDPLACE} they're pulling the planks off old barns to build with.
[us] Is timber that short there?
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} would buy every log you have, at any price you named.
[us] We'll keep that in mind.
[them] The log carts are coming to our town again.
[us] Your carpenters must be pleased.
[them] They're busier than they've been all year, and grumbling about it.
[them] We're holding {SITUATION} at {SITUATIONPLACE}, have you heard?
[us] We have, are you taking part?
[them,them:old] I'm too old for it now, but I'll be shouting from the side.
[them] Not this year, but everyone in the family is going to watch.
[us] I hope your people do well.
[them] So do I, though the champions from away are hard to beat.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} are holding {HEARD} at {HEARDPLACE} this season.
[us] Is it worth going to see?
[them] Champions are coming from all over, so it should be worth the walk.
[us] Maybe some of ours will try their luck.
[them] {ENDED} is over, and the town is still arguing about the results.
[us] Who came out best?
[them] Depends who you ask, and everyone has an opinion.
[them] Our people have proclaimed {SITUATION}, anyone outlawed may come home.
[us] Whatever they did?
[them] Whatever they did, as long as they come in peace before the season turns.
[us] Is everyone happy about that?
[them] The ones with someone coming home are, and the ones they wronged less so.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} have pardoned their outlaws, did you know?
[us] We'd heard something of it.
[them] The road is full of people walking home to {HEARDPLACE} who haven't seen it in years.
[us] That must be a strange homecoming.
[them] The time for the pardon has run out at home.
[us] Did many come back?
[them] More than anyone expected, and a few we'd all forgotten.
[them] It's {SITUATION} at {SITUATIONPLACE}, the young ones are all looking for places.
[us] Do most of them find one?
[them] Most do, the strong and the clever first.
[us] And the rest?
[them] They walk on to the next town, and the one after that.
[them] The young people on the road are walking to {HEARD} at {HEARDPLACE}.
[us] Looking for work?
[them] Work, a roof and a master who pays on time, if there is such a thing.
[us] We might have a place for the right one.
[them] The hiring is over at home for this season.
[us] Did the young ones find their places?
[them] Most of them, and the rest have gone further down the road to look.
[them] We keep {SITUATION} at {SITUATIONPLACE} this week.
[us] What do you do for it?
[them,their:tribal] We sit at the fire and the eldest tells how the first fire was lit.
[them,their:lowtech] There's a procession, the bells, and far too much to eat.
[them] Speeches, music, and a long table in the square.
[us] It sounds like a good day.
[them] The best of the year, and the town looks its best for it.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} are keeping their founding day at {HEARDPLACE}.
[us] Is it a big occasion?
[them] Big enough that they've asked every neighbor in good standing.
[us] We'll see whether we're on the list.
[them] Our founding day has come and gone for another year.
[us] Was it a good one?
[them,ended:helped] A good one, and your colony's part in it was noticed.
[them] A good one, though half the town needed a day to recover.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: The roads round {SITUATIONPLACE} have gone to mud.

lines.li: [them] The roads round {SITUATIONPLACE} are mud to the axles.
[us] How did you get here, then?
[them] On foot, mostly, the carts can't get through.
[us] You picked a hard week to travel.
[them] It wasn't my choice, the errand couldn't wait.
[them] Don't try the road toward {HEARDPLACE} just now, it's all mud.
[us] As bad as that?
[them] There are carts sunk to the hubs all along it, waiting for the sun.
[us] Thanks for the warning.
[them] The roads at home have dried out at last.
[us] Everyone back on the move?
[them] Everyone at once, so now the roads are jammed instead.
[them] Have you seen the stars falling these nights?
[us] I've heard of them, but I haven't been up at the right time.
[them] At {SITUATIONPLACE} we stay up half the night to watch them.
[us] Do your people make anything of it?
[them,their:seers] The readers are writing down every one, and arguing about what it means.
[them] Some say it means something, and the rest just like the view.
[them] They say one of the falling stars came down whole near {HEARDPLACE}.
[us] Has anyone found it?
[them] Half the town has been out in the hills looking for it.
[us] I'd like to see a piece of it.
[them] The stars have stopped falling over home.
[us] Do you miss watching them?
[them] I miss it, but I'm glad of a full night's sleep again.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {PEOPLE} are burying the old dead above {SITUATIONPLACE}.

lines.li: [them] We're burying the old dead the flood uncovered above {SITUATIONPLACE}.
[us] All of them?
[them] Every one, friend and enemy, nobody should lie in the open.
[us] That's hard work.
[them,their:sextons] It's the Bell's work, and we'll ring over every grave before we leave.
[them] It is, and it will take us weeks, but it's right that it's done.
[them] {HEARDPEOPLE} are burying a whole old battlefield above {HEARDPLACE}.
[us] We'd heard they were asking for linen.
[them] Linen, spades and anyone willing to dig, they'll take all three.
[us] It's a decent thing to do.
[them] The old field is quiet now, every grave dug.
[us] It must feel good to have it done.
[them] It does, and my back is glad of the rest.
[them] {SITUATION} at {SITUATIONPLACE} is down in the river.
[us] Can people still get across?
[them] On foot by the ferry, but the carts have to go the long way round.
[us] How long until there's a new one?
[them] The end of the season, if the timber comes in time.
[them] The bridge at {HEARDPLACE} is down, so I came the long way round.
[us] Is that why so many travelers are passing us?
[them] It is, the long way goes right past your land.
[us] We've noticed.
[them] The new bridge at home is open.
[us] Is it as good as the old one?
[them,ended:helped] Better, and some of its beams came from your colony.
[them] Better, the builders say, and it had better be.
